The New Horizons propulsion system includes 16 small hydrazine-propellant thrusters mounted across the spacecraft in eight locations, a fuel tank, and associated distribution plumbing. Four thrusters that each provide 4.4 newtons of force (1 pound) are used mostly for course corrections. I have tried making drinks in a blender but the drinks always come out far to weak or far too strong. I feel like I'm missing something here. I'm looking for advice.

When blending an alcoholic beverage, remember a few things. First, put ice in the Blender before you put in the ingredients, the same amount of ice as would fill the glass of the beverage you're making, maybe slightly less. You do this, (the ice first) because when you pour liquor over ice, it causes an actual chemical reaction, which imparts flavors to the drink. I was taught this by my first bar manager, several years ago. So, after ice, liquor first - and then any mixers/syrups, etc. Blend for about 15 seconds - just enough so that it's evenly blended, but not starting to become watery from having been overblended.
That makes sense. Thank you. I will try this as soon as I have bought some mixers.

As a simple rule one can say that a cocktail normally only consist of about 1/3 strong alcohol. Since you blend ice as well, you have to take these into account, considering the strength of your end product.

1. Fill the glass its going in with ice.
  2. add 2 oz/ 50 ml of 40% abv/ 80 Proof liquor
  3. Pour juice or any other liquids over ice in glass, fill it up.

Chuck it all from the glass into the blender and blend. this will give the right consistency and volume.

Remember, Alcohol does not freeze and will mess upo the consistency of your drink. So do not put more into it than specified unless its weak liqueur or such. The basics is that a 350 ml drink should have 20-30ml of pure alcohol in it nothing more. (50mlx 40%).
